quote: Theorem 3.1 For i = 1, 2, . . . , n, let Ti and Wi be two sets of mutually independent random variables with Ti ∼ LL(σ, λi) and Wi ∼ LL(σ, λi). Further, suppose that Ii (Ii*) be a set of independent Bernoulli rv, independent of Ti's (Wi's) with E(Ii) = pi (E(Ii*) = p*i), i = 1, 2, ..., n. If h : [0,1] → R+ is a differentiable and strictly convex function, then i) h(p) ≽w h(p*) implies Xn:n ≥st Yn:n if λ ∈ D+ (E+), h(p) ∈ D+ (E+), and h(u) is increasing in u; ii) h(p) ≽w h(p*) implies Xn:n ≥st Yn:n if λ ∈ D+ (E+), h(p) ∈ E+ (D+), and h(u) is decreasing in u, where h(p) = (h(p1), h(p2), . . . , h(pn)).
model: parallel systems with random shocks (Xi = Ii Ti mixture)
family: log-Lindley LL(σ, λi) components, common shape σ; Bernoulli shocks
compared: two systems under weak majorization of transformed shock vectors h(p)

hypotheses.text: h(p) ≽w h(p*) (weak supermajorization); monotonicity ordering of λ and h(p); h convex; h increasing (i) / decreasing (ii)

ambiguity: Majorized shock parameter vector yields larger system lifetime.

quote: Theorem 3.2 For i = 1, 2, . . . , n, let Ti and Wi be two sets of mutually independent random variables with Ti ∼ LL(σ, λi) and Wi ∼ LL(σ, δi). Further, suppose that Ii be a set of independent Bernoulli rvs with E(Ii) = pi, i = 1, 2, ..., n and h : [0,1] → R+ is a differentiable and strictly convex function. If i) either λ ∈ D+, h(p) ∈ D+ (E+), and h(u) is increasing (decreasing) in u, ii) or λ ∈ E+, h(p) ∈ E+ (D+), and h(u) is increasing (decreasing) in u, then v ≽w v* implies Xn:n ≥st Yn:n, where v = (1/(1+λ1σ), ..., 1/(1+λnσ)) and v* = (1/(1+δ1σ), ..., 1/(1+δnσ)).
model: parallel systems with random shocks, common shock vector
compared: two systems under weak majorization of transformed scale vectors v

hypotheses.text: v ≽w v*; ordering membership on λ, h(p); h convex monotone

ambiguity: Majorized scale vector leads to smaller system lifetime (λi larger ⇒ vi smaller ⇒ st-smaller maximum).

quote: Theorem 3.3 For i = 1, 2, . . . , n, let Ti and Wi be two sets of mutually independent random variables with Ti ∼ LL(σ, λi) and Wi ∼ LL(σ, δi). Further, suppose that Ii (Ii*) be a set of independent Bernoulli rvs with E(Ii) = pi (E(Ii*) = p*i), i = 1, 2, ..., n and h : [0,1] → R+ is a differentiable and strictly decreasing and convex function. If (v, h(p)) ∈ Un, and (v*, h(p*)) ∈ Un, then [h(p); v] ≻w [h(p*); v*] implies Xn:n ≥st Yn:n, where v = (1/(1+λ1σ), . . . , 1/(1+λnσ)) and v* = (1/(1+β1σ), . . . , 1/(1+βnσ)).
compared: two systems under row-wise weak majorization of the 2×n parameter matrix

hypotheses.text: (v, h(p)), (v*, h(p*)) ∈ Un (rows similarly ordered); matrix [h(p);v] weakly row-majorizes [h(p*);v*]; h strictly decreasing convex

quote: Counterexample 3.1 For σ = 0.5 and i = 1, 2, 3, let Ti ∼ LL(σ, λi) and Wi ∼ LL(σ, βi). Let (v1, v2, v3) = (0.4, 0.4, 0.1) and (v1*, v2*, v3*) = (0.5, 0.4, 0.2), where vi = 1/(1+λiσ) and vi* = 1/(1+βiσ). Now if h(p) = (2, 2, 1) and h(p*) = (3, 2, 1) are taken, where h(u) = −log(u), then it can be written that [h(p); v] ≻w [h(p*); v*], where (v, h(p)) ∈ Un and (v*, h(p*)) ∈ Un. The figure given below also shows that, for all 0 ≤ x ≤ 1, FX3:3(x) ≤ FY3:3(x) giving that X3:3 ≥st Y3:3.
compared: numerical confirmation of Theorem 3.3's matrix-majorization claim
ambiguity: Figure-based check of the CDF ordering on 0 ≤ x ≤ 1.

quote: Theorem 3.4 For i = 1, 2, . . . , n, let Ti and Wi be two sets of mutually independent random variables with Ti ∼ LL(σ, λi) and Wi ∼ LL(σ, δi). Further, suppose that Ii (Ii*) be a set of independent Bernoulli rvs with E(Ii) = pi (E(Ii*) = p*i), i = 1, 2, ..., n. compared: two systems under chain (strong) matrix majorization of the parameter matrix

hypotheses.text: matrix [h(p);v] chain-majorizes [h(p*);v*] (symbol ≻≻); h strictly decreasing convex
